# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Xu_2026_vancomycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Xu_2026_vancomycin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.01840-25>

Xu 2026 developed a vancomycin population PK model from routine therapeutic
drug monitoring in 626 children aged 3 months to 18 years at The Royal
Children's Hospital, Melbourne, validated it externally against three other
Australian children's hospitals, and used Monte Carlo simulation to propose an
age- and serum-creatinine-stratified dosing table targeting an AUC24-48 of
400-650 mg*h/L.

The model is a two-compartment model with the "standard" paediatric clearance
scaling: allometric weight scaling to a 70 kg adult, the Rhodin sigmoid
renal-maturation function of postmenstrual age (PMA), and a renal-function
factor built on the deviation of the measured serum creatinine from the value
expected for the child's age (Ceriotti):

$$CL = TVCL \cdot (WT/70)^{0.75} \cdot \frac{PMA^{3.4}}{PMA^{3.4} + 47.7^{3.4}} \cdot e^{-\theta_{SCR}(SCR - SCR_{std})}$$

$$SCR_{std} = -2.37330 - 12.91367 \ln(age) + 23.93581 \, age^{0.5}$$

with PMA in weeks, age in years and serum creatinine in umol/L.

# Population

```{r population}
pop <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Xu_2026_vancomycin"))$population
str(pop[c("n_subjects", "n_concentrations", "age_range", "age_median",
          "weight_range", "weight_median", "sex_female_pct")])
```

The development cohort (Table 1) contributed 3,687 concentrations from 626
children: median age 6.80 years (0.20-18.4), median weight 22.9 kg
(2.70-115), median PMA 397 weeks (39.4-998), median serum creatinine
31.0 umol/L (10.0-328), 55.0% male, 27.8% admitted to intensive care. Children
on ECMO, peritoneal dialysis or renal replacement therapy were excluded.
External validation used 35 children from Perth, 17 from Sydney Children's
Hospital and 170 from The Children's Hospital at Westmead.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Xu_2026_vancomycin.R`; the table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Two-compartment IV model, first-order elimination | n/a | Results 'Population pharmacokinetic modeling'; Table S2 final model |
| `lcl` (CL) | 7.56 L/h/70 kg | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V1) | 85.6 L/70 kg | Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q) | 1.30 L/h/70 kg | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (V2) | 286 L/70 kg | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Methods Equation 2; Results; Table 2 footnote equations |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Results; Table 2 footnote equations |
| Maturation function | n/a | Methods Equation 3; Table 2 footnote |
| `hill_mat` | 3.4 (fixed) | Table 2 'Hill' (from Rhodin 2009) |
| `tmat50` | 47.7 weeks (fixed) | Table 2 'TM50' (from Rhodin 2009) |
| Renal factor `exp(-theta * (SCR - SCRstd))` | n/a | Methods Equation 5; Table 2 footnote |
| `SCRstd` (Ceriotti) | n/a | Methods Equation 6 |
| `e_creat_cl` | 0.0188 per umol/L | Table 2 'Effect of creatinine on CL' |
| `etalcl` | 0.048841 (22.1% CV) | Table 2; CV = sqrt(omega^2) per Table S2 footnote |
| `etalvc` | 0.108241 (32.9% CV) | Table 2 |
| `etaiov_cl_*` | 0.034969 (18.7% CV) | Table 2 inter-occasion variability |
| `propSd` | 0.233 | Table 2; Table S2 'Prop.error' |

# Typical clearance throughout childhood (Figure 2)

Figure 2 plots the typical clearance standardised to 70 kg against PMA. At a
serum creatinine equal to the age-expected value the renal factor is 1, so the
standardised clearance is `TVCL` times the maturation function. The solve
below evaluates the packaged model (not a re-typed formula) for a 70 kg
subject along a PMA grid, with the creatinine set to the Ceriotti value for
the matching postnatal age of a term-born child.

```{r fig2}
mod <- readModelDb("Xu_2026_vancomycin")

ceriotti <- function(age_y) -2.37330 - 12.91367 * log(age_y) + 23.93581 * sqrt(age_y)

pma_grid <- tibble::tibble(PAGE = seq(41, 52.18 * 19, length.out = 120)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    time = dplyr::row_number() - 1,
    AGE = (PAGE - 40) / 52.18,
    WT = 70,
    CREAT = ceriotti(AGE),
    OCC = 1L
  )

# One subject whose covariates change at every (dose-free) observation row, so
# each row evaluates the clearance equations at one PMA.
ev_typ <- pma_grid |>
  dplyr::select(time, AGE, WT, CREAT, OCC, PAGE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central")

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::select(time, cl, vc, vp) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(pma_grid, time, PAGE), by = "time")
stopifnot(nrow(typ) == nrow(pma_grid))

ggplot(typ, aes(PAGE / 52.18, cl)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.8, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 18)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 20)) +
  labs(x = "PMA (years)", y = "Clearance (L/h/70 kg)",
       caption = "Replicates the typical-value line of Figure 2 of Xu 2026.")
```

```{r fig2-checks}
cl_at <- function(pma_weeks) {
  stats::approx(typ$PAGE, typ$cl, xout = pma_weeks)$y
}
cl_max <- 7.56
c(at_1y = cl_at(52.18), at_2y = cl_at(2 * 52.18), at_3y = cl_at(3 * 52.18),
  frac_2y = cl_at(2 * 52.18) / cl_max, frac_3y = cl_at(3 * 52.18) / cl_max)

# Deterministic typical values -- tight bounds are appropriate.
# Results: 'clearance reached 90% of its maximum value by 2 years PMA and
# subsequently plateaued after 3 years PMA'. Figure 2's line reads about
# 4.3 L/h/70 kg at 1 year PMA and about 3 L/h/70 kg at 0.8 years.
stopifnot(
  cl_at(2 * 52.18) / cl_max > 0.90,
  cl_at(3 * 52.18) / cl_max > 0.97,
  abs(cl_at(52.18) - 4.35) < 0.1,
  abs(cl_at(0.8 * 52.18) - 2.93) < 0.1,
  abs(max(typ$cl) - cl_max) < 0.01
)
```

The Discussion converts the 70 kg estimates to per-kilogram values: a typical
clearance of 0.108 L/h/kg and a total volume of distribution (V1 + V2) of
5.31 L/kg.

```{r per-kg}
adult <- typ[which.max(typ$PAGE), ]
per_kg <- c(cl = adult$cl / 70, vss = (adult$vc + adult$vp) / 70)
round(per_kg, 3)
stopifnot(abs(per_kg[["cl"]] - 0.108) < 0.0005, abs(per_kg[["vss"]] - 5.31) < 0.005)
```

The renal factor shrinks clearance by `exp(-0.0188)`, about 1.9%, for every
1 umol/L that serum creatinine exceeds the age-expected value: about 17% for
10 umol/L above it.

# Monte Carlo dosing simulation (Table 3 and Table S3)

Table 3 of Xu 2026 compares, for nine age-by-serum-creatinine subgroups, the
standard 15 mg/kg every 6 h with an optimised per-subgroup mg/kg dose (1-h
infusions throughout). It reports the probability of attaining an AUC24-48 of
400-650 mg*h/L (PTA) and the median trough concentration. Table S3 adds a
25 mg/kg loading dose before the optimised regimen.

The paper drew its 1,000 subjects per subgroup from its own multi-centre
covariate database, which is not published. The cohort below draws age and
serum creatinine uniformly within each subgroup's bounds and body weight from
an approximate sex-averaged median weight-for-age curve with log-normal
scatter. Postmenstrual age is postnatal age + 40 weeks (term birth). Each
virtual child receives inter-individual variability and one occasion's
inter-occasion variability on clearance.

```{r cohort}
subgroups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~grp, ~age_lo, ~age_hi, ~scr_lo, ~scr_hi, ~std_pta, ~std_trough, ~opt_dose, ~opt_pta, ~opt_trough, ~ld_pta,
  "3 mo-1 y, SCR 10-30",  0.25,  1, 10,  30, 10.5,  7.92, 22, 66.1, 11.86, 67.0,
  "1-4 y, SCR 10-30",     1,     4, 10,  30, 10.8,  7.82, 22, 65.9, 11.72, 63.0,
  "1-4 y, SCR 30-50",     1,     4, 30,  50, 47.6, 12.07, 19, 79.9, 15.14, 79.5,
  "4-10 y, SCR 20-40",    4,    10, 20,  40, 28.0,  9.58, 21, 76.6, 13.79, 74.4,
  "4-10 y, SCR 40-60",    4,    10, 40,  60, 66.5, 14.01, 16, 80.4, 15.56, 80.1,
  "10-16 y, SCR 30-60",  10,    16, 30,  60, 46.6, 11.96, 19, 71.9, 14.54, 71.1,
  "10-16 y, SCR 60-80",  10,    16, 60,  80, 72.3, 18.49, 13, 79.2, 16.31, 81.1,
  "16-18 y, SCR 50-80",  16,    18, 50,  80, 63.4, 14.41, 15, 70.6, 14.82, 72.9,
  "16-18 y, SCR 80-110", 16,    18, 80, 110, 47.1, 23.27, 10, 66.6, 15.85, 77.6
)

# Approximate sex-averaged median weight-for-age (kg) for a virtual cohort only.
wfa <- tibble::tibble(
  age = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18),
  wt  = c(6.0, 7.6, 9.5, 12.2, 16.3, 20.7, 25.6, 32.0, 40.5, 50.0, 58.0, 63.0)
)

n_per <- 100

# set.seed() seeds R's RNG for the covariate draw. rxode2's IIV / residual
# streams are partitioned per solver thread, so the simulated cohort differs
# between machines; every assertion below holds for any cohort the model can
# produce.
set.seed(20261113)
cohort <- subgroups |>
  dplyr::select(grp, age_lo, age_hi, scr_lo, scr_hi) |>
  dplyr::slice(rep(seq_len(dplyr::n()), each = n_per)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    AGE = stats::runif(dplyr::n(), age_lo, age_hi),
    CREAT = stats::runif(dplyr::n(), scr_lo, scr_hi),
    WT = stats::approx(wfa$age, wfa$wt, xout = AGE)$y *
      exp(stats::rnorm(dplyr::n(), 0, 0.15)),
    PAGE = 40 + AGE * 52.18,
    OCC = 1L,
    subj = dplyr::row_number()
  )

regimens <- subgroups |>
  dplyr::select(grp, opt_dose) |>
  tidyr::crossing(regimen = c("standard", "optimised", "loading")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(maint = ifelse(regimen == "standard", 15, opt_dose))

subjects <- cohort |>
  dplyr::inner_join(regimens, by = "grp", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
stopifnot(nrow(subjects) == nrow(subgroups) * n_per * 3)

dose_times <- seq(0, 42, by = 6)
doses <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mgkg = ifelse(regimen == "loading" & time == 0, 25, maint),
    amt = mgkg * WT,
    rate = amt / 1,
    evid = 1L
  )
obs <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 48, by = 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, AGE, CREAT, WT, PAGE, OCC) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
```

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261113)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

## AUC24-48 by PKNCA

```{r pknca}
# Only `!is.na(Cc)`: the grid starts at time 0, so the time-zero row is kept.
conc_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subjects, id, grp, regimen), by = "id")

dose_df <- doses |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, grp, regimen)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | regimen + grp + id,
                             concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + grp + id, doseu = "mg")

intervals <- data.frame(start = 24, end = 48, auclast = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, grp, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(nca) == nrow(subjects), !anyNA(nca$auclast))
```

The trough is taken as the concentration at 48 h, just before the ninth dose.

```{r pta}
trough48 <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 48) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::select(id, trough = Cc)

summ <- nca |>
  dplyr::left_join(trough48, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, grp) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    pta = 100 * mean(auclast >= 400 & auclast <= 650),
    trough_med = median(trough),
    auc_med = median(auclast),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pub <- subgroups |>
  dplyr::select(grp, std_pta, std_trough, opt_pta, opt_trough, ld_pta) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-grp, names_to = c("regimen", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(std|opt|ld)_(.*)") |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = dplyr::recode(regimen, std = "standard",
                                        opt = "optimised", ld = "loading"))

cmp <- summ |>
  dplyr::inner_join(pub, by = c("regimen", "grp"),
                    suffix = c("_sim", "_pub")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    regimen = factor(regimen, levels = c("standard", "optimised", "loading")),
    grp = factor(grp, levels = subgroups$grp)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(regimen, grp)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == 27)

cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pta_sim = round(pta_sim, 1),
    trough_med = round(trough_med, 2),
    auc_med = round(auc_med)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, grp, pta_pub, pta_sim, trough, trough_med, auc_med) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Regimen = regimen,
    Subgroup = grp,
    "Published PTA (%)" = pta_pub,
    "Simulated PTA (%)" = pta_sim,
    "Published median trough (mg/L)" = trough,
    "Simulated median trough (mg/L)" = trough_med,
    "Simulated median AUC24-48 (mg*h/L)" = auc_med
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Probability of AUC24-48 of 400-650 mg*h/L and median trough: Xu 2026",
    "Table 3 (standard and optimised q6h regimens) and Table S3 (25 mg/kg",
    "loading dose then the optimised regimen; no trough reported) against",
    n_per, "virtual children per cell."
  ))
```

```{r pta-checks}
pta_diff <- cmp$pta_sim - cmp$pta_pub
trough_ratio <- cmp$trough_med / cmp$trough
trough_ratio <- trough_ratio[!is.na(trough_ratio)]
c(median_pta_diff = median(pta_diff),
  p90_abs_pta_diff = unname(stats::quantile(abs(pta_diff), 0.9)),
  median_trough_ratio = median(trough_ratio),
  p90_abs_log_trough_ratio = unname(stats::quantile(abs(log(trough_ratio)), 0.9)))

# Cohort-derived, so the checks are on the centre and on a robust quantile, with
# headroom for Monte Carlo error (about 5 percentage points per cell at 100
# subjects) and for the cohort being reconstructed rather than the paper's own.
# A mis-transcribed clearance, a wrong creatinine sign or a wrong weight
# exponent moves the troughs by tens of percent and fails these at once.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(pta_diff)) < 10,
  stats::quantile(abs(pta_diff), 0.9) < 25,
  abs(log(median(trough_ratio))) < log(1.15),
  stats::quantile(abs(log(trough_ratio)), 0.9) < log(1.4)
)
```

```{r pta-plot, fig.height = 5}
cmp |>
  dplyr::select(regimen, grp, Published = pta_pub, Simulated = pta_sim) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Published, Simulated), names_to = "source", values_to = "PTA") |>
  ggplot(aes(grp, PTA, fill = source)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PTA, AUC24-48 400-650 mg*h/L (%)", fill = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the PTA columns of Table 3 and Table S3 of Xu 2026.") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Sign of the Ceriotti constant.** Methods Equation 6 writes the
  age-expected serum creatinine as `-2.37330 - 12.91367 ln(age) + 23.93581
  age^0.5`; the restated clearance equation under Table 2 prints the constant
  as `+2.37330`. The model uses Equation 6: it is the equation the Methods
  define and cite to Ceriotti, and every other published use of the Ceriotti
  equation checked by the maintainers (including deposited NONMEM code) carries
  `-2.37330`. The `+` in the Table 2 footnote is read as a typesetting slip.
  The two forms differ by 4.75 umol/L in the expected creatinine, about 9% in
  clearance.
- **Allometric exponents on Q and V2.** Supplemental Table S2 labels the
  weight exponent on V2 as 0.75 and on Q as 1, the reverse of the Results text
  ('CL, Q: 0.75; V1, V2: 1.0'), of the Table 2 units (Q in L/h/70 kg, V2 in
  L/70 kg) and of the Table 2 footnote equations. The model follows the main
  text and equations.
- **Number of occasions.** Inter-occasion variability on clearance is defined
  per treatment episode; the paper does not say how many occasions were
  modelled. Four occasions are provided (`OCC` 1-4); other values add no
  inter-occasion term. Occasions 2-4 share the occasion-1 variance, the
  equivalent of NONMEM `$OMEGA BLOCK(1) SAME`. Because rxode2 has no `| occ`
  variability level, the occasion etas are selected by indicators and cannot
  be mu-referenced: rxode2 prints "some etas defaulted to non-mu referenced"
  on every solve. That affects only the speed of a future estimation run, not
  simulation.
- **Age and creatinine outside the Ceriotti range.** The paper applies the
  Ceriotti expression across 3 months to 18 years without truncation, and the
  model does the same. `AGE` must be positive (the expression takes its log).
- **Postmenstrual age.** The paper does not say how PMA was derived when
  gestational age was unrecorded. The simulations here assume term birth
  (PMA = 40 weeks + postnatal age).
- **Virtual cohort.** The covariate database behind the published simulation
  is not available. Age and serum creatinine are drawn uniformly within each
  subgroup and weight from an approximate median weight-for-age curve with 15%
  log-normal scatter, so the cell-by-cell agreement is approximate. The
  simulation uses 100 children per cell, not the paper's 1,000. Doses are
  not capped. The paper does not state whether its simulation included
  inter-occasion variability; here each child carries one occasion's
  inter-occasion term in addition to inter-individual variability. The trough
  is the 48 h concentration.
- **Loading-dose timing.** Table S3 gives a 25 mg/kg loading dose followed
  by the optimised q6h regimen; the loading dose is placed at time 0 and the
  first maintenance dose at 6 h.
- **Development-cohort size.** The Results text reports 627 patients and
  Table 1 lists 626; the model metadata uses Table 1.
- **Covariates screened and not retained.** Sex, albumin, urea, ICU admission
  and central-line status were screened and no further covariate survived
  stepwise covariate modelling. An alternative maturation function with an
  O'Hanlon postnatal-age birth-transition factor (Table S2) fitted worse and
  is not part of the final model.
- **No published NCA.** Xu 2026 reports no non-compartmental parameters, so
  the validation compares against the paper's own simulated PTA and trough
  tables instead.
